title: Either branch operations, payload conversions and conditional composition
explanation: For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the thirty-five named APIs have the following value-model contracts. either dispatches only to the callback for the present variant, passing exactly its payload; either_with additionally passes the original context as the first pair element. either_into dispatches that payload to the corresponding Into dictionary. Their main contracts preserve the selected computation's whole modeled Result without assuming success. Separate normal-value contracts need success only at the selected payload/context; failure and divergence helpers retain the same modeled outcome. The unused callback/conversion dictionary is unconstrained. Twelve earlier callback APIs compose a mathematical callback under their explicit normal-result premises for every callback argument, with selected failure propagated and nonselected results preserved. The real impl<T> IntoEither for T dictionary is linked to its original default, so into_either_with requires only normal predicate behavior at the actual borrowed input. Predicates/projections identify and retain the exact variant and optional payload; flip swaps it and flipping twice reconstructs the original. Eager selection preserves the indicated payload or supplied alternative. Optional and tuple factoring preserve tags and exact components. as_ref preserves the borrowed view; as_mut's backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back. The original handwritten conversions map Result Ok to Right and Err to Left, with exact payloads, and reverse those mappings; both roundtrips reconstruct every variant. left_or_default/right_or_default preserve the matching payload without a Default premise and otherwise delegate the Default computation's entire modeled outcome. Normal fallback values, modeled failure and divergence have separate explicit premises. The earlier thirty APIs return normally in this model under their stated conditions; the Default fallback pair and the three dispatch APIs retain abstract selected-computation outcomes. These are value-semantic guarantees with the destructor and callback boundaries stated below.
trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library value models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are restricted to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are used. Generic FnOnce, Into and Default computations are explicit dictionary parameters; their concrete implementations and effects are not independently verified here. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value/backward-function semantics and do not independently prove the Rust borrow checker or aliasing model.

Thirty-five callable roots plus one actual blanket-implementation metadata root are extracted together into a single unchanged Generated.Either module; six proof modules and all thirty-five machine claims are jointly imported and audited.
limitations: Only the thirty-five mapped callables and their stated composition helpers are verified, not every public API. The new dispatch contracts establish branch/payload/context forwarding and modeled Result delegation, not arbitrary callback or Into correctness, success, termination, panic freedom or captured-state effects. Their normal-value theorems assume the selected call succeeds at that argument. No arbitrary mutable-context writeback or eager argument-construction claim is added. Rust Drop for discarded callbacks/payloads can panic, diverge or affect global state; destructor execution, unwind/return ordering, resource consumption and external effects are outside the value model. Modeled fail/div propagation is not a specification of every Rust panic payload or unwinding behavior. Default implementation values/termination/effects remain unverified. IntoEither uses the actual blanket dispatch, but its predicate/reference semantics retain the stated model boundary. Other inherent methods, iterator and pinning APIs, most trait/blanket implementations and serde remain unproved. into_inner still fails the untouched generated Lean do-match elaborator for the repeated T parameter; factor_ok/factor_err remain blocked by their current extraction/model limitations. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets are not proved.

Their main contracts preserve the selected computation's whole modeled Result without assuming success. Separate normal-value contracts need success only at the selected payload/context; failure and divergence helpers retain the same modeled outcome. The unused callback/conversion dictionary is unconstrained. Twelve earlier callback APIs compose a mathematical callback under their explicit normal-result premises for every callback argument, with selected failure propagated and nonselected results preserved. The real impl<T> IntoEither for T dictionary is linked to its original default, so into_either_with requires only normal predicate behavior at the actual borrowed input. Predicates/projections identify and retain the exact variant and optional payload; flip swaps it and flipping twice reconstructs the original. Eager selection preserves the indicated payload or supplied alternative. Optional and tuple factoring preserve tags and exact components. as_ref preserves the borrowed view; as_mut's backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back. The original handwritten conversions map Result Ok to Right and Err to Left, with exact payloads, and reverse those mappings; both roundtrips reconstruct every variant. left_or_default/right_or_default preserve the matching payload without a Default premise and otherwise delegate the Default computation's entire modeled outcome. Normal fallback values, modeled failure and divergence have separate explicit premises. The earlier thirty APIs return normally in this model under their stated conditions; the Default fallback pair and the three dispatch APIs retain abstract selected-computation outcomes. These are value-semantic guarantees with the destructor and callback boundaries stated below.
claims.shared_trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library value models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are restricted to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are used. Generic FnOnce, Into and Default computations are explicit dictionary parameters; their concrete implementations and effects are not independently verified here. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value/backward-function semantics and do not independently prove the Rust borrow checker or aliasing model.
claims.shared_limitations: Only the thirty-five mapped callables and their stated composition helpers are verified, not every public API. The new dispatch contracts establish branch/payload/context forwarding and modeled Result delegation, not arbitrary callback or Into correctness, success, termination, panic freedom or captured-state effects. Their normal-value theorems assume the selected call succeeds at that argument. No arbitrary mutable-context writeback or eager argument-construction claim is added. Rust Drop for discarded callbacks/payloads can panic, diverge or affect global state; destructor execution, unwind/return ordering, resource consumption and external effects are outside the value model. Modeled fail/div propagation is not a specification of every Rust panic payload or unwinding behavior. Default implementation values/termination/effects remain unverified. IntoEither uses the actual blanket dispatch, but its predicate/reference semantics retain the stated model boundary. Other inherent methods, iterator and pinning APIs, most trait/blanket implementations and serde remain unproved. into_inner still fails the untouched generated Lean do-match elaborator for the repeated T parameter; factor_ok/factor_err remain blocked by their current extraction/model limitations. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets are not proved.
